title: Alvarez: rousing grace is sufficient, operating grace efficacious
source_text: LX. Similiter Alvares gratiam excitantem distinguit ab operante: quoniam gratia excitans ipsi est gratia quaedam voluntatem ad bonum moraliter tantum trahens & alliciens. Operans vero, gratia non solum moraliter, sed etiam physice voluntatem ad bonum praemovens & praedeterminans. Adeoque, juxta ipsum, gratia excitans eadem est cum gratia sufficiente. Gratia vero operans & cooperans pertinent ad gratiam efficacem.
pass_a_gloss: LX. Similarly Alvarez distinguishes rousing grace from operating: since rousing grace to him is a certain grace drawing and alluring the will to good only morally. But operating, a grace not only morally, but also physically premoving and predetermining the will to good. And so, according to him, rousing grace is the same as sufficient grace. But operating and cooperating grace pertain to efficacious grace.
pass_b_english: Thesis LX. Alvarez likewise distinguishes rousing grace from operating grace. For him rousing grace is a grace that draws and attracts the will toward good only morally, while operating grace not only morally but also physically premoves and predetermines the will toward good.
So on his view rousing grace is the same as sufficient grace, whereas operating and cooperating grace belong to efficacious grace.
